item.title: Libya recovers Swiss, Austrian women kidnapped since 2025 in Niger
item.description: Two women — one Swiss and the other Austrian — were released from more than a year of captivity in Niger and arrived in Libya’s eastern city of Benghazi, Libyan media outlets reported on Thursday. The two women — Swiss national Eva Gretzmacher, 76, and Austrian Claudia Abbt, 69 — were abducted in Niger in 2025. In a video released by Libya’s eastern-based al-Masar TV, the women appeared emaciated and thanked the country’s eastern-based military commander Khalifa Haftar and his son, Saddam, for their release. Al-Masar said “two hostages, an Austrian and a Swiss national, have been freed after being held captive in Niger for a year and a half”. “My name is Eva Gretzmacher, I am 76, and I thank from the bottom of my heart Marshal Haftar and his son, Saddam, who released us,” one of the woman said in French. “I had been held hostage for a year and nine months,” she said. Abbt said she was “happy to be free”, also thanking Haftar. Online website Libyan News Observatory also reported their release. Libya has struggled to recover from the chaos that followed the 2011 NATO-backed uprising that toppled longtime ruler Muammar Gaddafi. Two governments are currently vying for power: a UN-recognised administration in Tripoli led by Prime Minister Abdulhamid Dbeibah and its rival in the east backed by Haftar. item.title: Websites down: what is PHP and how has it raised AI hacking fears?
item.description: Artificial intelligence has found critical security flaws in a major programming language called PHP, with many websites taken offline Thursday as organisations worldwide scramble to fend off would-be hackers. As AI’s fast-advancing capabilities fuel concern over the increased risk of cyberattacks, here are some questions and answers about the situation: What is PHP and how widely used is it? Created in the early 1990s, PHP is a computer programming language that helps run an estimated 70 percent of the world’s websites. It is “a backbone of the web”, according to security firm Wiz Research, which says it used AI to find vulnerabilities hidden in PHP for more than a decade. PHP — a name that originally stood for Personal Home Page — underpins popular web design platforms, meaning the flaws could allow hackers to break into various sites, from online stores to government services. A fix was released Wednesday, with the PHP Foundation telling the tech departments of companies and organisations around the world: “If you run PHP, it is imperative that you update now.” That has resulted in a slew of apps and websites — from the Paris police website to a Pokemon sleep tracker — going dark as developers work to protect their underlying code from hacks. How did AI find the flaws? Cutting-edge AI models, such as those from US giants OpenAI and Google, were used by Wiz and other groups to uncover PHP’s weak spots in August. This was kept under wraps while a fix was developed. OpenAI called the flaws “one of the most impactful vulnerabilities in recent memory”, adding that it “marks a new phase, where AI can find security bugs with internet-scale impact”. item.title: Ebola: UN expresses confidence in Nigeria’s containment efforts
item.description: The United Nations has expressed confidence in Nigeria’s capacity to contain its newly confirmed Ebola case, pledging support to prevent further spread of the deadly disease. UN Secretary-General’s Spokesperson, Stéphane Dujarric, gave the assurance on Wednesday while responding to questions from the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) at the UN Headquarters in New York. Dujarric said the UN was concerned about the detection of the Ebola Bundibugyo virus in Nigeria, the fifth country to report a case during the current outbreak. However, he expressed confidence in Nigeria’s health authorities, commending their swift response and extensive contact-tracing efforts following the confirmation. “We have full confidence in the ability and the capacity of the Nigerian Government’s health authorities to deal with this single case,” he said. The spokesperson acknowledged that the appearance of the virus in another country raised concerns about its potential spread beyond countries already affected. “Yeah, I mean, it’s of course concerning that there is a case in a new country,” Dujarric said. He, however, noted that Nigerian authorities had already undertaken active contact tracing to identify and monitor people potentially exposed to the infected patient. item.title: Kano will vote Tinubu in 2027, Yusuf assures
item.description: By Hadiza Yusuf Kano State Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf has assured President Bola Tinubu of the support of Kano residents in the 2027 general election, expressing confidence that they will vote for the President to ensure the continuation of his development projects. Yusuf spoke on Wednesday while representing Tinubu at the commissioning of a section of the Abuja-Kaduna-Zaria-Kano Highway at Tamburawa, Kano State. He praised the President for projects being executed by the Federal Government, saying the highway would ease transportation across Northern Nigeria. The governor also said several projects executed by the Tinubu administration had not received adequate publicity. “I have seen many projects the President has executed that have not been publicised. I could go on and on listing the projects and initiatives of this administration,” Yusuf said. He expressed confidence that residents of Kano and other parts of the country would support Tinubu in the next general election. “The people of Kano will come out en masse to vote for President Tinubu, not only in Kano but across the North-West, the South and the country at large, to ensure the continuation of his development projects,” he added. Umahi Says Economic Hardship Easing Also speaking at the event, the Minister of Works, David Umahi, said the worst of Nigeria’s economic hardship was over, insisting that the Tinubu administration’s reforms were beginning to yield positive results. “The reforms have started to yield dividends of democracy. Even in the darkest hour before dawn, there is hope. Let us support President Bola Tinubu,” Umahi said. He cited road projects in Kano and other parts of the North-West as evidence of the administration’s efforts, adding that the Federal Government was working to complete projects inherited from the late President Muhammadu Buhari. “There is no project started by the late President Buhari that President Bola Tinubu is not doing in the North,” he said. Umahi listed several road projects in the region, including the Kano Northern Bypass, Kano Ring Road, Kano-Kongolam road and Zaria-Hunkuyi road projects. He also said the Federal Government was working on the Sokoto-Zamfara-Zaria road. According to the minister, some inherited projects have been redesigned to feature reinforced concrete pavement. Umahi said the Tinubu administration had completed close to 400 kilometres of roads in the North-West within three years, while about 4,000 kilometres of road projects were ongoing in the region. He added that the Abuja-Kaduna-Zaria-Kano Highway would benefit not only the North-West but also other parts of the country. item.title: North-South Power Rotation Fundamental For National Unity — Akume
item.description: The Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Senator George Akume, has reiterated the need for political stakeholders to respect the power rotation arrangement between Northern and Southern Nigeria, describing it as a fundamental understanding that has sustained national cohesion, fairness and the growth of democracy since the return to civilian rule in 1999. The SGF made the call while receiving a delegation from the Order of the Knights of St. Mulumba (KSM) Nigeria, led by its Supreme Knight, Sir Steve Adehi, on Wednesday in Abuja, according to a statement by his Head, Information & Public Relations, Chris Ugwuegbulam. He recalled that the agreement was reached in Kaduna in 1999 following extensive consultations between governors-elect on the platform of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and prominent political leaders who recognised the need for equitable distribution of political power to preserve Nigeria’s unity. Akume said the leaders eventually agreed that presidential power should alternate between the North and the South in eight-year cycles, beginning with the South, as a practical measure to promote political balance, strengthen mutual trust and safeguard the country’s territorial integrity. According to him, the discussions were driven by concerns over the concentration of political power in one part of the country and the growing dissatisfaction among stakeholders who believed that a deliberate arrangement was necessary to ensure fairness and national inclusion. The SGF noted that the arrangement has contributed to the continuity of democratic governance by providing a framework for managing the country’s regional diversity and ensuring that neither part of the country feels permanently excluded from the highest political office. He stressed that the principle of power rotation should not be treated as a temporary political convenience but as an important political understanding rooted in the need for fairness, mutual respect and national stability. item.title: Delta traditional rulers mourn Uduaghan
item.description: The Delta State Council of Traditional Rulers has mourned former Governor Emmanuel Ewetan Uduaghan, describing him as a detribalised leader whose legacy of peace, development and support for traditional institutions would endure. The council, in a condolence message dated October 21, 2026, extended its sympathies to the Uduaghan family of Abigborodo, Governor Sheriff Oborevwori and the people of Delta State over the former governor’s death. The message was signed by the Chairman of the council, the Orodje of Okpe Kingdom, HRM Orhue I, CFR, MNI. The traditional rulers said the news of Uduaghan’s death was received with shock and profound bewilderment, recalling his cordial relationship with the traditional institution during his tenure as governor. According to the council, Uduaghan prioritised the welfare of traditional rulers and made significant contributions to human capital development, infrastructure and the promotion of peace among the state’s ethnic groups. It described the former governor as a detribalised leader who treated all parts of Delta as one indivisible family, irrespective of ethnic differences. The council noted that although Uduaghan inherited the Warri crisis from his predecessor, he worked to establish lasting peace among the three warring ethnic groups. It said his contributions would continue to resonate among Deltans, particularly his efforts to strengthen the traditional institution and enhance its standing alongside similar institutions in other states. The council prayed for the repose of Uduaghan’s soul and other departed faithful, while asking God to comfort his immediate family, the Delta State Government and the people of the state over what it described as an irreparable loss. item.title: Yobe court sentences man to death for killing wife
item.description: By Maryam Abdul-aziz Usman A Yobe State High Court sitting in Damaturu has sentenced a 45-year-old man, Abubakar Musa, popularly known as Daddy, to death by hanging for the killing of his wife, Ammi Adamu Mamman. Musa was arrested on January 4, 2024, following his wife’s death at New Bra-Bra Estate, Damaturu, and was subsequently charged with culpable homicide, according to media reports. The then Police Public Relations Officer of the Yobe State Command, DSP Dungus Abdulkarim, said the incident occurred at about 4:48 a.m. on January 4, after the ‘C’ Divisional Police Headquarters in Damaturu received a distress call. Abdulkarim said the couple were on the same bed when Mamman was allegedly attacked with a sharp object on the neck, causing severe bleeding that led to her death. He said Musa was arrested for interrogation, while the homicide unit of the State Criminal Investigation Department commenced an investigation into the circumstances surrounding the incident. The case subsequently went to High Court 1 in Damaturu, where the judge reportedly held that the prosecution had proved its case beyond reasonable doubt. University Community Mourned Deceased Mamman’s death also drew reactions from the university community. A February 2024 newsletter published by Yobe State University identified her as a member of staff and said the Vice-Chancellor, Professor Mala Mohammed Daura, mourned her death and called on security agencies to ensure that those responsible were brought to justice. The university described her death as a loss to its community. She was buried in Potiskum on January 9, 2024, according to the newsletter. The Women-led Civil Society Organizations Network in Yobe State also condemned the killing and called for justice. In a statement issued shortly after the incident, the network identified the deceased as Ammi Adamu Mamman and said she was a volunteer with one of its member organisations. Yobe State Governor, Mai Mala Buni, also expressed condolences to the family and called on security agencies to establish the circumstances surrounding her death, assuring that anyone found responsible would face the law. A lawyer quoted in media reports said Musa retained the right to appeal the judgment within the period prescribed by law. item.title: Maradona doctor was made ‘scapegoat’ for his death, court told
item.description: A lawyer for Leopoldo Luque, a doctor charged in the 2020 death of Argentine football legend Diego Maradona, said in closing arguments Wednesday that his client was innocent and had been made a “scapegoat.” Attorney Roberto Rallin rejected the prosecution’s argument that Maradona’s November 2020 death was foreseeable, while another defense attorney, Francisco Oneto, maintained that his death resulted from an “acute and unpredictable” heart attack. “There was absolutely no possibility of predicting this fatal outcome,” Oneto insisted. Prosecutors have requested a 12-year prison sentence for Luque, a neurosurgeon considered a key decision-maker for Maradona at the time of his death. “We are here to proclaim Luque’s innocence, not with television slogans, but with the evidence that supports it,” Rallin said. “Leopoldo Luque has been the scapegoat.” Maradona died at age 60 from a cardiorespiratory crisis coupled with pulmonary edema. He was found dead in his bed at a residence in Tigre, north of Buenos Aires, rented for his convalescence, following surgery for a subdural hematoma. The death of Argentina’s favorite son plunged the country into mourning in the midst of the Covid-19 pandemic. Tens of thousands of people defied social distancing rules to bid farewell to him as he lay in state at the presidential palace. A total of seven health-care professionals have been on trial since April for potential negligence leading to the star’s death during his two weeks of convalescence. Prosecutors have requested sentences ranging from four to 12 years for six of the seven defendants. item.title: Amnesty Int’l demands release of journalist jailed over comments on police
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi Amnesty International has demanded the immediate release of 23-year-old journalist Farida Isiak, who was sentenced to four years in prison or a fine of N1.75 million over a Facebook post criticising the police in Kaduna State. The human rights organisation said her arrest and punishment “were clearly because of her attempt to expose abuses by the police.” “Sentencing a journalist to 4-years in prison after a sham trial is a travesty of justice,” it said. Isiak, a reporter with Nagarta Radio in Kaduna, was reportedly taken into custody around 10pm on October 20 by officers under the command of the Divisional Police Officer of Mararaban Jos, Usman Adamu. According to the global rights group, the case began as a minor disagreement between her mother and a neighbour over N100 change during a sale of charcoal. Police first arrested her mother, then detained her father when he went to secure her release, “using their detention as leverage to force Farida to come to the police station.” At the station, officers accused her of defaming them over a Facebook post in which she criticised their unlawful treatment of her parents. Following pressure by the police, she deleted the post and apologised, hoping it would secure her parents’ release. The officers instead kept her in custody and took her to a Sharia Court in Kawo. The presiding judge sentenced her to four years in prison or a fine of N1.75 million for defamation, “completely ignoring the initial police misconduct and the abusive actions that led to the incident.” Amnesty International said: “The arrest, detention, and hasty sentencing of Farida Isiak are a flagrant abuse of power by the police and weaponization of the judicial system to silence free speech and intimidate journalists.” It added that “arresting and holding a citizen’s parents to force a journalist to hand herself over is an unlawful tactic that violates rule of law. Demanding accountability for police actions is a constitutional right”. It called on the Kaduna State Police Command and Nigerian judicial authorities to “immediately release Farida Isiak, drop all charges, and cancel the fine imposed on her.” The organisation also urged the Nigeria Police Force to launch a full and independent investigation into the conduct of the officers involved in the unlawful detention of her family. “Nigerian authorities must stop using defamation charges and the legal system to harass journalists and restrict press freedom,” it said. item.title: Fernandes takes aim at Carrick as Man Utd lurch into fresh crisis
item.description: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes criticised manager Michael Carrick’s tactics following the humiliating 4-1 Champions League defeat at Como. United fell behind to a second-minute goal and never recovered as the club’s winless run reached seven games after another lacklustre performance. “We started on the wrong foot and they scored very early,” Fernandes told TNT Sports. “Not much pressure on the ball, not many good movements with the ball, not many things going our way.” The Portugal midfielder suggested Nico Paz’s early strike for Como on Wednesday night had a damaging effect on the visitors, leaving them struggling to impose themselves. Paz scored again after Tasos Douvikas had doubled the lead, with Jacobo Ramon adding a fourth. Only a stoppage-time goal from Joshua Zirkzee stopped United from succumbing to their joint-heaviest Champions League loss. “Conceding early makes us go into the game with a mood of defeat,” said Fernandes. “It’s difficult to get out of that, trying to be brave, to have the ball and make something happen. “If we are not able to do that, it is going to be very difficult to get out of this situation.” Fernandes also highlighted United’s passive approach out of possession, saying Como were allowed too much time and space to dictate play. Asked whether those comments amounted to criticism of Carrick’s tactics, Fernandes said: “That’s on the manager and staff to see, not me. “Sometimes you have to be more brave under pressure, take the risk of pressing high and making them uncomfortable.” Fernandes is the latest United player to publicly break ranks. Defender Lisandro Martinez took aim at the club’s hierarchy following a 2-0 Champions League loss to Atletico Madrid last week. Martinez said Carrick had been left with an understrength squad. He later apologised. Youri Tielemans, who started alongside Fernandes in the United midfield in Italy, admitted the display was simply not good enough. “We got outplayed for most of the game so it was a very disappointing night,” said Tielemans. “You can be good tactically but if the effort is not good (then it will not work) and vice versa. You need to be good at everything and tonight we were poor.” AFP The post Fernandes takes aim at Carrick as Man Utd lurch into fresh crisis appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Cardoso puts Nigerian financial markets at centre of deeper investment ties with China
item.description: Central Bank of Nigeria Governor Olayemi Cardoso has identified investment in Nigerian financial markets, including naira-denominated instruments, as a key opportunity to deepen financial ties with China. During discussions with the chairman and senior management of the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC), Cardoso outlined how greater participation by Chinese financial institutions could broaden the relationship between the two economies. He said Nigeria’s stronger financial foundations provided a more predictable environment for investment and enterprise. The priority was to consolidate stability and translate it into deeper markets, stronger investment and sustainable economic growth. “Our ambition is not simply to make financial transactions between Nigeria and China easier. It is to create the conditions for more transactions, greater investment and stronger financial flows in both directions,” he said. Cardoso identified greater participation by Chinese financial institutions in Nigerian markets as a practical opportunity to broaden the relationship. “We believe there is considerable scope to broaden this relationship, particularly by encouraging greater participation by Chinese financial institutions in Nigeria’s markets, including investment in naira-denominated instruments,” he said. The Governor outlined a role for ICBC in connecting its institutional networks with Nigerian investment opportunities. Its corporate relationships and international reach could help identify barriers to participation and translate commercial interest into financial activity. Nigeria and China already have substantial commercial ties. Cardoso said CBN data showed significant trade-related payments from Nigeria to China, alongside comparatively limited export proceeds and investment flows into Nigeria. Broader financial-market participation would add an investment dimension to a relationship heavily shaped by trade payments. Cardoso also set out the CBN’s responsibility: maintaining a credible, transparent and well-functioning financial environment, while working with counterparts to address regulatory and institutional barriers where appropriate. He proposed practical priorities and designated teams to carry the discussions forward. The measure of success, he said, would be greater transaction volumes, broader market participation and a more balanced financial relationship. item.title: Landing cost of petrol falls to N1,283.81/litre
item.description: •As crude oil rises to $108.90 per barrel By Ediri Ejoh The landing cost of imported Premium Motor Spirit, PMS, also known as petrol, has dropped marginally to N1,283.81 per litre from N1,292.88 per litre. The latest figure was disclosed by the Major Energies Marketers Association of Nigeria, MEMAN, in its energy bulletin yesterday. The decline came as Brent crude rose marginally to $108.90 per barrel from $108.80 per barrel, according to figures contained in the report. The latest landing cost is N66.19, or about 4.90 per cent, below Dangote Refinery’s gantry price of N1,350 per litre. Similarly, the landing cost of imported petrol was between N64.19 and N74.19 per litre below the ex-depot prices of N1,348 to N1,358 quoted by depot owners. Despite the decline in landing cost, petrol prices remained elevated in parts of the country, with motorists in Lagos and Abuja reportedly paying between N1,370 and N1,429 per litre at filling stations. The difference between landing costs and pump prices reflects additional costs and margins across the supply chain, including transportation, storage and retail operations. The development comes amid the Federal Government’s proposed 30-day petrol discount at NNPC Limited filling stations. Recall that the Minister of Finance, Taiwo Oyedele, on October 8 proposed that petrol be sold at N1,350 per litre at NNPC Limited outlets under the planned discount initiative. However, the proposed discount had yet to be implemented at NNPC Limited filling stations as of the time of reporting. item.title: 2027: Atiku lacks expertise to fix Nigeria’s economy — APC National Secretary
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The National Secretary of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Ajibola Bashiru, has questioned former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar’s expertise to fix Nigeria’s economy, saying President Bola Tinubu is addressing the country’s economic challenges while predicting that Nigerians will reject Atiku in the 2027 presidential election. Bashiru spoke on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Wednesday, while responding to questions about Atiku’s political ambitions and whether the former vice-president poses a threat to the ruling party ahead of the 2027 general election. “Atiku is not a professional, please, with respect to him. Atiku trained as an hygiene expert at the school of hygiene in Kano, He is a ‘wole wole’ man and went to be a tax collector in Customs. Where is the expertise? What has he done? Check his profile?” Bashiru said. He argued that holding the office of vice-president did not automatically make Atiku an expert on the economy. “So, the fact that you became a Vice President doesn’t make you an expert, what is his expertise?” he asked. Bashiru also linked Atiku to the economic difficulties the Tinubu administration is addressing, arguing that the former vice-president was among those responsible for the challenges facing the country. “If there are challenges that is being addressed by President Tinubu, one of the main people that caused it is Atiku Abubakar,” he said. Asked whether Atiku posed a threat to the APC, Bashiru described the former vice-president’s latest presidential ambition as his final attempt, predicting that Nigerians would reject him. “Atiku is the Oginga Odinga of our country and that is what the Vice president said. The keynote, on behalf of the Inspector-General of Police, Mr. Tunji Disu, was delivered by the Lagos State Commissioner of Police, Mr. Fatai Tijani. But beyond titles and protocol, the message was one: Nigeria must stop waiting for the next abduction before it acts. The Chairperson’s Warning: Don’t stop at the press statement. Prof. Ogundipe, as chairperson, set the tone. He did not want another conference of communiques. He challenged education journalists to change the way school safety is reported. “When authorities announce new security measures, our reporting should not end with the announcement. When funds are allocated, we should investigate whether they are used as intended, and when investigations produce recommendations, we should return to determine what has changed,” he said. “Our ultimate objective is not to embarrass institutions. It is to ensure that they fulfil their responsibilities.” For a country where security votes and intervention funds often disappear into vague budget lines, it was a pointed call for accountability journalism. “Children are not safe until every school is safe” If Ogundipe gave the framework, EWAN Chairman, Mojeed Alabi, gave the conscience. Standing before his colleagues, Alabi began with a line that would echo through the hall all day: Children are not safe until every school is safe. “No parent should have to choose between a child’s education and their safety. No teacher should have to teach under the shadow of abduction, and no community should have to watch its future disappear because its schools have become targets,” he said. In a deeply personal address titled: Why Journalism Matters in the Fight Against Violent Attacks on Schools, Alabi traced the pattern Nigerians have come to know too well: an attack happens, government issues a statement, security agencies announce interventions, public outrage rises, then attention moves elsewhere – until the next attack. “We must therefore ask: how many more warnings, disrupted school terms and grieving families will it take before school safety becomes an unquestionable national priority?” he asked. item.title: Ebola: Atiku challenges Tinubu to account for N10bn
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has challenged President Bola Tinubu to account for the N10 billion announced for Ebola preparedness, alleging that the confirmed case in Abuja exposed serious gaps in surveillance and the protection of health workers. Atiku said the government must explain how the emergency funds were spent and why the response allegedly left frontline health workers without adequate protective equipment. He also warned against using the outbreak to restrict political campaigns and voter participation. In a statement by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, on Wednesday, Atiku demanded a public audit of the funds and answers over the handling of the case. “Where is the money? Publish the amount actually disbursed, the dates of payment, every contract awarded, every recipient and every item delivered. A press statement cannot replace an audit,” he said. Atiku said the patient arrived in Nigeria on October 5, developed symptoms on October 7 and sought treatment at a private hospital on October 11, but the government did not publicly confirm the case until October 20. “During that critical period, 44 close contacts were left unmonitored, while private health workers faced the case without adequate protective equipment. This is a failure of preparedness with potentially grave consequences,” he said. He also questioned the Presidential Task Force announced by Tinubu in June and chaired by his Chief of Staff, Femi Gbajabiamila, insisting that medical experts should lead the response. “Political titles cannot trace contacts, equip hospitals or save lives,” Atiku said. The former vice president further alleged that the planned press conference by the Minister of Health on Thursday was intended to discourage Nigerians from attending campaign rallies and voting. “The Tinubu administration must not weaponise Ebola to frighten the public, silence its opponents or suppress voter participation. Any public health measure must be backed by clear medical evidence, applied equally and never used as a pretext to interfere with Nigerians’ democratic rights,” he said. Atiku urged the government to account for the N10 billion, protect health workers and trace all contacts, warning against turning a public health emergency into a tool for political suppression. item.title: Insurance firms’ N300b stuck at CBN over verification for illicit funds
item.description: By Rosemary Iwunze Insurance companies are now struggling to have access to the new capital they raised, amounting to about N300 billion under the just concluded recapitalization programme. The funds were held in the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, pending verifications for illicit funds inflows. Vanguard learnt that following suspicion of possible illicit sources of some of the new investments in the firms the apex imposed stricter capital verification regime, a development which has proved tough for most of the insurance firms to scale through. It is further learnt that while the National Insurance Commission, NAICOM, has given approval for the apex bank to release the funds to the insurers, the affected firms are painstakingly going through the processes. Speaking to journalist during the virtual press briefing on the outcome of the Insurers Committee meeting, Chairman of Nigeria Insurers Association, NIA, Mrs. Ebelechukwu Nwachukwu, stated that, the insurance sector regulator has done its part while operators are currently working on the CBN criteria to access the funds on or before the end of this month. The insurers said they had planned to deploy the new capital in the third quarter of this year to boost their financial performance in 2026 while rewarding their investors with good returns in dividend for their support in the recapitalization program. Recall that the 24 insurance companies had cumulatively raised N300 billion during the exercise, added to over N700 billion existing capital, taking the total industry capital to N1.079 trillion, post recapitalisation. The Nigerian Insurance Industry Reform Act (NIIRA), 2025, had stipulated that the underwriting firms and reinsurers who participated in the recapitalisation exercise that ended on July 31st, 2026 must keep their recapitalised funds in an escrow account with CBN. item.title: Real Madrid Rout Leipzig, Continue Perfect European Start

Their fourth consecutive win across all competitions will boost Madrid’s morale ahead of Sunday’s La Liga Clasico against bitter rivals Barcelona. Without a major trophy for two seasons and having endured a shaky domestic start, Madrid can at least boast a perfect record in Europe, unlike Barca after their defeat at Paris Saint-Germain on Tuesday. Mourinho started with Vinicius, serving a four-match ban in La Liga, on the left flank and benched former Leipzig winger Diomande, despite his improving form.
